tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on P5 Circuit Basics

questions.question: Foundation Name the component that measures current and state how it is connected in a circuit.
questions.correctAnswer: An ammeter measures current. It is connected in series with the component — the current flows through it.

questions.question: Foundation A resistor has 8 V across it and a current of 2 A flows through it. Calculate its resistance.
Foundation Describe the difference between the I-V graph of a resistor and a filament lamp.
questions.correctAnswer: A resistor (at constant temperature) gives a straight line through the origin — current is directly proportional to voltage (Ohmic). A filament lamp gives a curved graph that flattens at higher voltages — as current increases, the filament heats up and resistance increases, so current increases more slowly (non-Ohmic).

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on P5 Circuit Basics

questions.question: Higher A thermistor is connected to a 5 V supply. At 25 °C its resistance is 1000 Ω. At 100 °C its resistance is 100 Ω. Calculate the current at each temperature and explain the difference.
questions.correctAnswer: At 25 °C: I = 5 / 1000 = 0.005 A = 5 mA. At 100 °C: I = 5 / 100 = 0.05 A = 50 mA. The current is much higher at 100 °C because the thermistor's resistance decreases as temperature increases (more charge carriers are released), allowing more current to flow.

questions.question: Higher Explain why a diode only allows current to flow in one direction. How would this appear on an I-V graph?
questions.correctAnswer: A diode has very low resistance in the forward direction (allows current through) but very high resistance in the reverse direction (blocks current). On the I-V graph: there is current in the forward direction (positive voltage), rising steeply once the threshold voltage is exceeded. In the reverse direction (negative voltage), the current is essentially zero.

questions.question: Higher A student investigates the I-V characteristics of a resistor. They vary the voltage and measure the current. State one safety precaution and one way to improve accuracy.
questions.correctAnswer: Safety precaution: do not exceed the maximum voltage rating of the resistor to avoid overheating/burning out. Improving accuracy: take multiple readings and calculate a mean, or use smaller voltage increments to get more data points for a smoother graph.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on P5 Circuit Basics

questions.question: Extended Answer 6 marks: Compare the I-V characteristics of a resistor, a filament lamp and a diode. Include descriptions of the graph shapes and explanations for each. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A resistor at constant temperature is an Ohmic conductor. Its I-V graph is a straight line through the origin, meaning current is directly proportional to voltage. The resistance remains constant. A filament lamp is a non-Ohmic conductor. Its I-V graph is a curve that flattens at higher voltages. As current increases, the filament heats up, the metal ions vibrate more, and resistance increases, so current increases less quickly. A diode only allows current to flow in the forward direction (forward bias). On the I-V graph, current is zero in reverse bias and rises steeply once the threshold voltage (~0.6 V) is exceeded in forward bias. The diode has very high resistance in reverse and very low resistance in forward bias above the threshold. Mark scheme: 1 mark — resistor straight line / Ohmic, 1 mark — resistance constant, 1 mark — lamp curves / non-Ohmic, 1 mark — resistance increases with temperature, 1 mark — diode conducts in one direction only, 1 mark — reference to threshold voltage or very high reverse resistance
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
